q1_pattern_verified.xeoxo_note: Xéo Xọ (VN mass áo dài, CHEAP) = ~60% branded (branded_type=all share-of-total; 'xéo xọ' alone = 43.5% of clicks). HIGHER branded than pricier Shanghai Tang (44%) / Qipology (13%). → BREAKS the clean price→branded story: the real driver is brand FAME/recall, not price. A cheap-but-cult brand is name-driven; a pricier-but-obscure one is category-driven. Strategic reframe: Maison must MANUFACTURE recall (press/celebrity/social), not rely on price tier.

q1_pattern_verified.vn_set_reading: VN designer/couture brands = name-driven (75-100% branded); VN mass áo dài (Hà Cúc 44%) = category-driven ('áo dài + location/type'). Xéo Xọ (60%) > Hà Cúc (44%) because of cult-fame. Confirms: designer ⇒ own the NAME; generic 'áo dài …' terms = the mass brands' turf. Caveat: 4 of 8 (Phương My/Thuỷ/La Hằng/Vũ Việt Hà) have tiny organic volume → directional not precise.
q1_pattern_verified.reading: Discovery is NAME-DRIVEN when a brand has RECALL/fame (couture usually does; Xéo Xọ shows a cheap brand can too). Category head-terms cap <5% for famous brands; category/product search dominates only OBSCURE brands (Qipology 87% non-branded). Lever = fame, not price. NO CONFLICT with SEO: still do brand-name SEO + product SEO on SPECIFIC demand terms (wedding guest dress / modern ao dai / áo dài cưới); only skip GENERIC head-terms (luxury/designer dress) where cheap mass retailers dominate.
q1_pattern_verified.channel_reading: Organic + Direct = 78-88% owned-intent. Paid thin BUT present at bridal houses fighting occasion terms (Galia 13.1%, Elie 10.6% paid search) + accessible-luxury (Shanghai Tang). Cong Tri channels GATED (404).
q1_pattern_verified.geo_reading: US #1 near-universal (couture 45-61%); VN #2 for both VN analogs (29-32%) = the Maison fingerprint. Elie Saab outlier (MENA/S-Asia heritage). Shanghai Tang (sub-$2000) breaks US-#1 (SG home market).

wedding_seasonality_proxy_2025-06_to_202._method: SimilarWeb keyword-trend endpoints hard-cap at 3 months → cannot show 12-mo seasonality curve. PROXY = monthly website visits (allows long windows) of 2 big wedding-attire retailers, worldwide total. NOT keyword search volume; US-centric retailers = Western/N-hemisphere season.
wedding_seasonality_proxy_2025-06_to_202.reading: Both: trough Oct-Dec → sharp climb from Jan → peak Mar-Apr → high through spring. Driver = engagement season (Nov-Feb proposals) → dress shopping Jan-Apr. 'wedding guest dress' keyword (US) still rising Apr→May (67K→83K) → guest-dress buying peaks later (into summer). ACTION: publish wedding content/collection late-year (Oct-Dec) to catch the Jan-Apr surge.
caveats: proxy = site traffic not search volume
VN 'áo dài cưới' seasonality (likely Oct-Dec + post-Tết) NOT measured — hard 3-mo keyword cap
